review_comment: The added Function(src) call executes JavaScript code directly from the src parameter without validation beyond syntax checking. This creates a code injection vulnerability where any valid JavaScript in the src parameter will execute with the application's privileges. Replace the Function constructor with a safe parsing approach that validates the content structure or use a sandboxed execution environment with restricted capabilities.

The error message construction accesses source code lines using parser-reported line numbers without bounds validation. When the line number exceeds the actual number of lines in the source code, this results in reading beyond the array bounds. Add bounds checking before the array access to ensure this.line - 1 is within the valid range of src.split('\n').

The added esprima.parse() call processes user-controlled JavaScript code without size or complexity limits, creating a potential denial-of-service vector. While the Function() constructor provides some syntax validation, it doesn't prevent resource exhaustion attacks. Implement input size limits and consider adding timeout mechanisms for parser operations to mitigate resource consumption risks.
